title: Framework grows up
sub: Generics, WPF, LINQ, async, version by version
cards/0/title: Every version was a big step
cards/0/body: Framework and C# grew together. Almost every release brought something you can hardly imagine C# without today.
cards/1/body: List<int> instead of ArrayList: the compiler checks the type, and numbers are not boxed into objects. Generics live in the CLR itself, not just in the language. Java does it differently.
cards/2/body:
3.0: WPF (a new XAML-based UI), WCF (network services), Workflow Foundation.

3.5 and C# 3.0: LINQ, lambdas, var, extension methods. Queries over collections and databases, written in plain C#.
cards/3/body:
4.0: the Task Parallel Library, TPL (Task, Parallel.For), and dynamic.

4.5 and C# 5: async and await. Asynchronous code that reads like ordinary code.
cards/4/task: Find the year async and await arrived in C#.
cards/5/explain: Each feature built on the ones before it: LINQ needs generics and lambdas, and async needs Task.
cards/6/q: Match each version to its headline feature
cards/7/q: How do .NET generics differ from Java generics?
cards/7/options/0: They exist in the runtime itself: List<int> stores real ints with no boxing
cards/7/explain: Java erases generics at compile time, so List<Integer> stores objects.
cards/8/explain: await waits on a task. Task came first, and two years later C# got a convenient syntax for it.
